description: Needs a free TronRelic account: calling it makes your app ask the user to sign in, then the call runs. Search PUBLISHED blog posts by free text, newest first, as lightweight summaries (no body). The query is a case-insensitive literal substring matched against each post's title, tags, and markdown body — not a boolean or fuzzy query, so search a distinctive word or phrase (e.g. "energy rental"), not a full question. Use when looking for posts about a specific topic; use list-blog-posts instead to browse everything or select by date. Read-only; never mutates. Parameters: "query" (required, 1-200 characters), "page" (optional, 1-based, default 1), "limit" (optional, default 20, clamped to 50). Returns { success, posts: [{ id, slug, title, tags, excerpt, publishedAt }], total, page, limit } — "total" counts every match for paging, and each "id" can be passed to get-blog-post to read the full markdown body. Only published posts are ever returned; zero matches returns an empty list (not an error). This searches blog posts only, never site pages. A blog post is dated writing about something that happened or a time-bound analysis: it is listed newest first at /blog/<slug> and may be published to outside channels. A standing reference page kept current at a fixed address, such as a guide, explainer, policy, or documentation, is a site page, not a blog post; use the pages tools (pages-search, pages-get, pages-propose-edit, pages-propose-page) for those.

limit.description: Page size (optional, default 20); clamped to the range 1-50.

page.description: 1-based page number (optional, default 1). Values below 1 are treated as 1.

query.description: The text to find (required, 1-200 characters); matched case-insensitively as a literal substring of the title, tags, or body.

name: search-blog-posts
title: Search blog posts
